title: Essentially smooth DVR point criterion for Néron lft-models
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A commutative group scheme over a base has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over that base satisfying the commutative group identities. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $N$ be a smooth separated $S$-group scheme, locally of finite type, with finite-type generic fibre $G$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then the following are equivalent: (i) for every smooth $S$-scheme $X$, restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_K(X_K,G)$ [def-pc-base-change]; (ii) for every local injective extension of discrete valuation rings $R\to A$ for which $A$ is a local ring at a point of a smooth $R$-scheme, restriction $N(A)\to G(\operatorname{Frac}A)$ is surjective. Thus (i) says that $N$ is a Néron lft-model of $G$. Neither quasi-compactness of $N$ nor excellence, completeness or perfection of residue fields is required.

proof.text: Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. The DVR definition makes $R$ Noetherian; [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] gives dimension one. The only primes are $(0)$ and the maximal ideal: an intermediate nonzero prime would give a chain of length two. Thus its prime localizations are the field $K$ and $R$ itself, both regular local by the generator definition [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Hence $R$ is regular and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. For any smooth $S$-scheme $Y$, its affine smooth charts are regular by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent], and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. Thus every stalk of $Y$ is a Noetherian normal domain. Moreover $Y$ is reduced, locally Noetherian and $Y_K$ is dense by [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback], applied to the reduced locally Noetherian $S$ and its dense generic open.

proof.text: Every point of such a $Y$ has an integral affine open neighbourhood. Indeed take a regular affine smooth chart. It is a Noetherian scheme; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] gives the descending-chain condition on closed subsets. Its normality from step 1 allows [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components]: its components are disjoint open-and-closed normal integral schemes. The component containing the chosen point is affine (the complementary open-and-closed decomposition of an affine scheme corresponds to an idempotent). This last assertion can also be avoided by taking any affine open inside that open component. In particular, on this neighbourhood the fraction field of its coordinate ring equals the fraction field of the stalk at any point, by the localization description [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization].

source.place: Tag 0357 (lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves) for affine stalks.

proof.text: Assume (i), and let $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ be a DVR as in (ii), with fraction field $F$. The structural image of $\pi$ is nonzero and is in the maximal ideal of $A$, since $R\to A$ is injective and local. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], writing it as a unit times a positive power of a uniformizer of $A$ shows $A[1/\pi]=F$. The same node gives $R[1/\pi]=K$. Given $a\in G(F)$, view it as a map to $N$ and choose an affine smooth chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $N$ containing its image. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] its coordinate algebra has a finite presentation over either $R$ or the generic affine open $K$ of $S$.

source.place: BLR §10.1 Proposition 2, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), with its local arguments expanded.

proof.text: Choose the integral affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $y$ from step 2 and its prime $\mathfrak q$. Then $A=B_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. For each of the finitely many generators of $C$, its image in $F=B_{\mathfrak q}[1/\pi]$ is $b/(s\pi^n)$ with $s\notin\mathfrak q$. Invert the product of these finitely many $s$ in $B$. Each of the finitely many defining relations vanishes after further localization at $B\setminus\mathfrak q$, so another finite product outside $\mathfrak q$ kills all their numerators. We obtain an algebra map $C\to B_t[1/\pi]$, $t\notin\mathfrak q$, and thus a morphism $(W_t)_K\to G$ inducing $a$. Apply (i) to the smooth open $W_t$, and restrict its extension $W_t\to N$ along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to W_t$. Its restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is $a$. This proves (ii).

source.place: BLR §10.1 Proposition 2, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), with its local arguments expanded.

proof.text: Assume (ii) and fix a smooth $S$-scheme $X$ and $f_K:X_K\to G$. For every point $x$ of the special fibre whose ambient local ring has dimension one, step 1 and [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] make $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ a DVR. The map $R\to A$ is local and injective. For injectivity, [lem-pc-smooth-flat] makes it flat; for $0\ne r\in R$, tensoring the injection $R\xrightarrow{r}R$ with $A$ makes multiplication by $r$ on $A$ injective. Since the local ring $A$ is nonzero, the image of $r$ cannot be zero. Thus (ii) applies to the point of $G(\operatorname{Frac}A)$ obtained from $f_K$, and provides $h_x:\operatorname{Spec}A\to N$ extending that point.

source.place: BLR §10.1 Proposition 2, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), with its local arguments expanded.

proof.text: Spread $h_x$ to an open neighbourhood of $x$ explicitly. A morphism from the spectrum of a local ring factors through every open neighbourhood of the image of its closed point: the inverse image is open containing that closed point and therefore all of the local spectrum. Choose an affine smooth chart $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq N$ at that image, with $C$ finitely presented over $R$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Inside an integral affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$ from step 2, use $A=B_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Represent the images of the finitely many generators of $C$ by fractions with denominators outside $\mathfrak q$, then invert their product; invert another product outside $\mathfrak q$ annihilating the finitely many relation numerators. This gives $h:W_t\to N$ inducing $h_x$ and with $x\in W_t$. On the generic fibre of this integral neighbourhood, $h$ and $f_K$ agree at its generic point, because its function field is $\operatorname{Frac}A$. By [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] they agree on all of $(W_t)_K$: this source is reduced, the generic point has dense image, and $G=N_K$ is separated. The last separatedness follows by base-changing the closed diagonal of $N$; on affine charts a closed immersion is a quotient, and tensoring a quotient is a quotient.

source.place: BLR §10.1 Proposition 2, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), with its local arguments expanded.

proof.text: Glue $f_K$ and all the maps $h$ of step 6 on the union $U$ of their domains and $X_K$. On every overlap their restrictions agree on its generic fibre, which is dense and reduced by step 1 applied to that smooth open. Hence [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] gives equality on the entire overlap, and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] produces $u:U\to N$ over $S$. It contains $X_K$ and every point of the special fibre with ambient local-ring dimension one. There are no dimension-zero ambient points over the closed point: their stalks are domains by step 1, and the injective local map from $R$ sends $\pi$ to a nonzero nonunit, whereas a zero-dimensional local domain is a field. Thus $U$ contains every point of $X$ of ambient codimension at most one.

source.place: BLR §10.1 Proposition 2, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), with its local arguments expanded.

proof.text: The open $U$ is dense in every fibre. Its generic fibre is all of $X_K$. If $x$ is a generic point of a component of $X_k$, its fibre local ring has dimension zero: in an affine fibre chart its prime is minimal, so localizing has only one prime. The flat local dimension formula [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula], applicable to the Noetherian stalks by step 1 and [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and the fibre-stalk identification [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient] give $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim R+0=1$. Hence all these generic points lie in $U$ by step 7. They are dense in $X_k$, since every point of an affine fibre chart specializes from a minimal prime. This proves the fibrewise density, including the case of empty fibres.

source.place: BLR §10.1 Proposition 2, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), with its local arguments expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-group-weil-extension] to $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the smooth $X$, the smooth separated group $N$, and $u:U\to N$. The base is normal Noetherian by step 1, fibrewise density is step 8, and the dimension-at-most-one condition is step 7. Obtain $f:X\to N$ extending $f_K$. For any two such extensions, $X$ is reduced and $X_K\subseteq X$ is dense by step 1, so [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] proves their equality. This proves the bijection (i). All constructions were on individual affine neighbourhoods followed by gluing; there was no finiteness assumption on the number of neighbourhoods or on $N$. If $X$ is empty both Hom sets have one element.
